pages.title: Heat Out, Air In
pages.text: The ORSA Heat Vent is an airtight radiator. It removes heat without losing oxygen or using fuel. A thermostat in the same sealed room opens the shutters above target and closes them at target. More vents add cooling capacity without cooling past the target.
Six iron ingots, two copper ingots and one lever. Installs as a full wall or roof block.

pages.title: Placement & Controls
pages.text: Place it while looking toward the outdoors: the fins point away from you. The opposite face must touch the room. Every vent needs its own unobstructed outdoor sky column; roofs, blocks and neighboring rooms prevent cooling. Without a thermostat, right-click toggles the shutter and redstone holds it open. A thermostat takes control of both.

pages.title: ORSA Service Grille
pages.text: The indoor service grille has a shutter lever and a status light. Dim means closed. Green means heat can leave to colder outdoors. Amber means open but waiting or obstructed. The light updates once per second. Slats in the grille do not let oxygen escape.

pages.title: Cooling Has Limits
pages.text: Heat flows only toward a colder exterior. The vent cannot cool below that exterior temperature. It cools room air first; stored wall heat continues warming the air. A depleted room loses wall heat instead. Larger rooms cool more slowly; several vents add cooling capacity.

pages.title: Avoid Wasting Fuel
pages.text: Install a $(l:heating/thermostat)thermostat$(/l) to control heating and cooling together. Heaters save fuel when machines supply enough warmth. One vent has conductance18 before the vacuum factor; two give36. Cooling depends on the temperature difference, so hot exterior conditions reduce its output. A manual open vent can waste heater fuel; thermostat control closes it when cool.
